rationale: A defensible consolidation of the archive's two strongest legs (stock-level cash cycle and debt-netted supplier-credit flow) whose expression matches the stated hypothesis, but it is an ensemble of already-validated components rather than new economics, so the main risk is that the averaged score simply inherits — and dilutes — the parents' alpha rather than adding non-redundant information.

The expression cleanly implements the stated asset-side decomposition of the winning cash-cycle signal and is a genuinely informative attribution test, though note the mechanical overlap with the profitability leg (high GP/AT already tilts toward asset-light firms), which risks the result being a partially self-reinforcing turnover effect rather than an earnings-quality one.

The proposal itself concedes that the asset-scaled version of operating liability leverage was already flagged as a Penman–Nissim rediscovery, and switching the deflator from assets to sales is a rescaling rather than a new construct; it also inherits a sign ambiguity, since high non-debt current liabilities per dollar of sales can indicate stretched or distressed payment behavior as easily as negotiated funding power.

NEG(DELTA(NOWC/sale)) is the classic working-capital accrual measure with a sales rather than asset deflator, and the archive already tested gross-profitability-times-working-capital-accrual constructs (GrossProfitVsWorkingCapitalPressure, ProfitPremiumWeightedByAccrualQuality) with weak portfolio evidence, making this a near-duplicate rediscovery of both a published anomaly and prior archive work.

Recasting the self-financing cycle as a coverage ratio is a real functional-form change rather than a pure rescaling and the hypothesis matches the expression's direction, but the economics are identical to the archive's best signal and the ratio is fragile for firms with near-zero non-cash current assets, so incremental information is plausible but not assured.

This is a three-year moving average of the leading archive signal's accrual leg with no other change — the definition of a cosmetic variant — and since balance-sheet working-capital ratios are already highly persistent, the smoothing will mostly reproduce the existing signal at slightly lower coverage rather than test a distinct economic claim.
